what_its_for: Eptinezumab-jjmr is used to prevent migraines in adults. It belongs to a group of medicines called CGRP antagonists. It works by blocking a protein in your body called CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide) that plays a big role in causing migraines. This medicine helps reduce how often you get migraines, but it is not used to treat a migraine once it has already started.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an infusion (a slow injection into your vein) by a doctor or nurse in a clinic or healthcare setting. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion takes about 30 minutes. You will sit or lie down comfortably while the medicine is slowly given through an IV (intravenous) line in your arm. You do not need to do anything special to prepare for the infusion, but let your healthcare team know about all medicines and supplements you take.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg given once every 3 months (every 12 weeks). Your doctor may increase your dose to 300 mg every 3 months if needed. Your doctor will decide which dose is best for you based on how well your migraines are controlled. Each treatment is given only once every 3 months, so you will only visit the clinic for infusions about 4 times a year.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule your infusion appointment, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to set up a new appointment. Try to stay on your every-3-month schedule as closely as you can. Do not try to give yourself this medicine at home under any circumstances.
storage: You will not need to store this medicine at home, as it is prepared and given to you in a healthcare clinic or infusion center. The medication is stored by healthcare professionals in a refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). It should be protected from light and should not be frozen. If you ever receive any supplies related to this medicine, keep them away from children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements, before starting this medicine. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after your infusion if you feel dizzy or unwell. There are no specific foods or drinks known to interact with this medicine, but always follow your doctor's general health advice. Do not stop any other migraine medicines without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience any of the following after your infusion: trouble breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, rash or hives, dizziness, or feeling like you might faint — these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction. Also contact your doctor if you notice: redness, swelling, or pain at the IV site, your migraines are not getting better or are getting worse, you develop a new rash or skin reaction, or you have any unusual symptoms that concern you. Always let all of your healthcare providers know you are receiving this medicine.
when_it_works: Many people notice fewer migraines within the first month after their first infusion. Some people may feel a difference even within the first week. Because everyone is different, it may take a few infusion cycles (a few months) to see the full benefit. Keep all of your scheduled infusion appointments even if you do not notice improvement right away, and talk to your doctor if you have concerns about how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): This medicine can be used in older adults. No special dose change is needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy: It is not known if this medicine is safe to use during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, think you might be pregnant, or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while using this medicine. Kidney or liver problems: No dose changes are typically needed for mild to moderate kidney or liver problems, but your doctor will decide what is best for your situation. Children: This medicine has not been studied in children and is only approved for use in adults.
